anīca: [Na+nīca] (ti) CL=8 Not being inferior, not being humble / belittle, not being ignoble
anīcatā: [Anica+tā] (thī) CL=8 The state of not being inferior. See also Alīnatā
anīcavutti: [Anīca+vutti] (ti) CL=8 The person who has the attitude of not being humble. See also Appatissa
anīgha: [Na+nīgha] (ti) CL=8 Na+ ī gha. The word  ī is also found as Anigha by means of Chanaḥrassa in some places. See the below format] 1) A) The person who does not have any trouble B) The person who does not have the trouble of strong desire C) The person who does not have the trouble of evil desire D) The person who does not have the trouble of evil desire, evil consequences of evil deeds. E) The person who does not have the Dhamma which tourtures like strong desire F) The person who does not have the trouble of evil consequences of evil deeds in the future 2) The state of having any trouble, not having any trouble. 3) The lesser Buddha who attained enlightenment but did not preach named Anīgha
anīhamāna: [Na+īhamāna] (ti) CL=0 Do not try to do it. he.
anīhatadosa: [Na+nīhata+dosa] (ti) CL=9 Having the defect-impurity that is not taken out/ removed; having the thick black stain that is not taken out. See Aniddhantakasāva. See also Anapanītakasāva.
anīka: [Ana+īka] (pu,na) CL=9 Anityanena ana+īkana, senāya, tassa hi jīvanarakkhakattā. Vācappati and Thoma. See also Uṇādi, 4.17. In Dhān ṭī.381 and Pācit, Yojanā-1.82, it is decided that this word is with Ṇa.] The army of elephants, of cavalry, of chariots and infantry. Army.
anīkaṭṭha: [Anīka+ṭhā+a.(anikasta-saṃ)] (pu) CL=9 stationed in an army of elephants. he, Military serviceman: (a) Elephant trainer, horse trainer, etc. (b) King"s bodyguard-army.
anītiha: [(1)anu+īti+hana+kvi.(2)na+īti+hanu+kvi.(3)na+ītiha.(၎)na+itiha(=iti+ha)] (ti) CL=9 Itiha-saddo nipātasamudāyo, itiha pubbācariyehi vuttamidanti katetabbaṃ vacanaṃ etihyaṃ, ṇyo, ṇamhi etihaṃ. Dhānaṭī.၎12.(See also itihāsa). Iti=evaṃ, ha=kira.] (1) gets rid of dangers. (2) having no impurities such as Taṇhā. (3) being opposite to heretical view; being not the view of heretics. (4) being not hearsay "thus said, thus happened". Being not fable; being self a experienced undoubtedly; having no other thing to believe.
anītika: [Na+īti+ka] (ti) CL=9 In Dhānaṭī, it is also considered as na + nīti +ka.] (A) Having no danger (īti). (B) Where there is no danger of defilement; (Nibbāna). (C) where there is no īti called Kilesa, khandhā, Abhisaṅkhāra; (Nibbāna). (D) where there is no īti called danger; (Nibbāna). (E) having no danger/ (Nibbāna). (F) where there is no decline-ruin- no fruitlessness; ( Nibbāna).
anītikadhamma: [Anītika+dhamma] (pu,na) CL=0 (A) The Dhamma which is the cause of this lack of danger, (Nibb )na). (B) The concept of the absence of suffering, (Nibb )na).
anītikadhammagāmī: [Anītikadhamma+gamu+ṇī] (ti) CL=8 The meaning of - not having any trouble - facing towards Nirvana -. See also Anītikadhamma -(kha)-
anītikadhammasutta: [Anītikadhamma+sutta] (na) CL=8 The Sutta which preaches about Nirvana where there is no trouble and the practice to - face towards - reach - Nirvana. Anītikamadhamma Sutta
anītikagāmī: [Anītika+gamu+ṇī] (ti) CL=8 Can lead to Nirvana where there is no trouble. See also Anītika -(ṅa)-
anītikasutta: [Anītika+sutta] (na) CL=8 The Sutta which preaches about Nirvana where there is no trouble and the practice to - reach - face towards - Nirvana. Anītika Sutta.
anītisampadā: [Anīti+sampadā] (thī) CL=8 Fully endowed with the state of being free from the danger of living things such as small insects (all sizes of insects)
anīḷaka: [Na+ela+ka] (ti) CL=8 Pārā, kaṇṭhisaca, In 2.359 it is said as NatthiI Ilaṃ Etthāti Anilakaṃ. Aneḷaka, Nīlakahāpaṇa comparing with the sun and moon.] Not haiving any sins, not having any bees, not having the sins which is as small as a bee or bee egg, being innocent. See also Aneḷaka
